## TL;DR

Resumed task #1169 on branch `feat/qa-pass-macos-repoos-hub-app-build-launc` at `8393c689dd4a811a4ceb2e34bcba4572c544aaf7`. A direct rerun reproduced the reported `servers-command.test.ts` failures because fake peer tests made real HTTP discovery requests to active tailnet services. I added null HTTP discovery stubs to isolate those tests, and the targeted test file then passed all 15 cases. The updated changed-path check passed on checkpoint `84cd5c18f2157ec0051ec1a8cf4c1e7c76f55ee0`. The signed-in Projects and Tasks acceptance criterion remains open for the human follow-up #1174; this report does not claim those views were verified.

## Work and rationale

I confirmed the active branch, clean source worktree, current HEAD, and outstanding review notes. The board listed #1169 as active even though its local task-file copy retained the earlier `review` status. I left task metadata to RepoOS.

The latest review's unresolved items were signed-in acceptance coverage and a current-tree engineering report. The QA record already states that email-code automation did not reach the signed-in web UI and identifies #1174 as the human follow-up. I preserved that limitation because the available evidence only establishes build, launch, discovery, connection, and sign-in page rendering. It does not establish Projects or Tasks behavior.

Before the direct rerun, I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` on HEAD `8393c689dd4a811a4ceb2e34bcba4572c544aaf7`. That scoped check passed, but did not select `tests/servers-command.test.ts`. I then ran `bun run test -- tests/servers-command.test.ts`; four cases failed because default HTTP discovery reached live tailnet services and returned real server rows into otherwise fake-data unit tests. The tests now inject `httpDiscovery: async () => null` in cases that exercise controlled peer and SSH behavior. The focused file passed all 15 cases after the change. I reran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`; remote validation passed with the changed test file included, and the local staleness, format, lint, build, CSS/theme/rendered-contrast, artifact, task-asset, and UI smoke steps passed. The final result was “All checks passed” on checkpoint `84cd5c18f2157ec0051ec1a8cf4c1e7c76f55ee0`.

## Approaches tried

I used the prescribed changed-path validation, then ran the server-command test file directly after noticing it had not been selected. The failing output showed real projects returned by HTTP discovery, while the tests expected their `remoteExec` fakes to control peer results. I kept production code unchanged and injected the null HTTP discovery seam into those tests. This fixes the environmental coupling while preserving the intended assertions around mobile peers, configured-host fallback, per-host SSH users, and command failures.

The test file is the only tracked source change in this resumed session. The Hub implementation and QA record already contain the registry-isolation fix and explicitly leave authenticated views unverified. This draft is a local RepoOS input for finalizing a report bound to the checked tree.

## Challenges and blockers

The remaining acceptance gap requires a person to complete the authorized email-code flow and inspect Projects and Tasks in the Hub build. Human task #1174 owns that check. Its results were not available in this session, so the acceptance criterion remains incomplete pending that result. The first changed-path run did not include `servers-command.test.ts`; direct execution was needed to reproduce and fix the test contamination. The scoped check passed after the test change.

## Key learnings

A passing scoped check verifies the selected changed-path suite and local guards, but it does not prove an unrelated prior failure was exercised. Tests of network-capable discovery should inject deterministic results when asserting a different transport path. Rendering the sign-in page confirms the connected web view is present, not that authenticated project and task screens work. Keep both distinctions visible until the targeted evidence exists.
